language.howToChooseYourGradeContent:
It’s very important children start at the right level, have fun in learning and work at their own pace. Please help the children selecting the level that is not too easy, but also not too difficult for them. There are two ways to do this.

  • You can either check the learning goals yourself to determine the correct level for your child(ren).
  • Or you can let the child take several lessons to determine his or her level. For example, if your child has the age of 6, please let him or her take one lesson in grade K, one lesson in grade 1, and one lesson in grade 2 to determine at which level he or she is.

dialog.text: Hi! I am John. I am travelling through the Atlantic ocean, along with my friend Jessi.
This morning I wanted to go for an under water dive for the first time. I was scared; the water was really cold. But Jessi gave me a water suit and told me that it will keep my body warm.
She told me that cold water conducts heat away from the body. Heat always flows from a substance at higher temperature to a substance at a lower temperature,
raising the temperature of the latter and lowering that of the former. So, in this case, the heat of my body would flow away into the cold ocean. Making me colder and the ocean a little bit warmer.
That's why I wear a wetsuit! Wetsuits slow heat loss with their thick layer of rubber. Let's see how that works....

Now we know that heat is a type of energy and it can be transferred from one object to another. This happens because of the difference in temperature between them. Given enough time, the temperatures of the two objects will become equal. Think about hot soup. If you wait too long before eating, it has become cold.

What do you know about solids, liquids, gases and some molecular formations?
In solids, like metal, the atoms are tightly connected together, so they transfer heat energy very easily from one atom to another, and thus they are often good conductors.
However, not all solids are good conductors. Atoms of gases are loosely bound, so they are poor conductors of heat.
